items.title: Four-velocity and four-acceleration of a future timelike worldline
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with proper-time function tau and inverse rho: J -> I (def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (a) The four-velocity of x is the map U: I -> V defined by U(s) := x'(s)/tau'(s) = c x'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); equivalently U(s) is the tangent at parameter value s of the proper-time parametrized worldline x o rho, read at the proper-time parameter tau(s). U is continuous, U(s) is future timelike for every s, and U does not depend on the base point chosen for tau. (b) If x is C^2, that is, x' is differentiable with continuous derivative, the four-acceleration of x is the map A: I -> V defined by A(s) := U'(s)/tau'(s) = c U'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); equivalently A is the derivative of the four-velocity with respect to the proper-time parameter along the worldline. A is continuous. (c) The dimensionless four-velocity of x is u := U/c. A point observer of the model at an event is a future unit timelike vector n in V, eta(n,n) = -1; the four-velocity of the observer's own worldline is cn at each of its events. (d) The names four-velocity and four-acceleration are the model's names for U and A; the physical interpretation, including the units in which U and A are measured, is supplied with the model's coordinate conventions and is not part of the affine geometry. The definition makes no claim that U has norm -c^2 or that A is orthogonal to U; those are proved in thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition.
items.strategy: Definition item: it introduces the two derived vector fields along a worldline and fixes their well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the division by tau'(s) is legitimate because tau' > 0 by lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization; (ii) the identification U(s) = (x o rho)'(tau(s)) is the chain rule applied componentwise in an inertial chart (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule), and it shows that U is the tangent field of the proper-time parametrized worldline; (iii) continuity of U follows from continuity of x' and tau' and continuity of division by the positive function tau'; (iv) A is defined only when x is C^2, in which case U' exists; (v) neither the norm of U nor the orthogonality of A with U is asserted here, so the definition cannot be used as if those identities were definitional. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Norms of four-velocity and four-acceleration, and the observer rest-space decomposition
items.statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^2 for every s in I; equivalently the dimensionless four-velocity u = U/c satisfies eta(u,u) = -1, and U(s) is future timelike. Thus the four-velocity of a worldline lies on the future unit hyperboloid. (b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration. If x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0: the four-acceleration has no component along the four-velocity; if in addition A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) is spacelike. (c) Rest space and projection. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Then n^perp is a 3-dimensional linear subspace of V, the restriction of eta to n^perp is positive definite, and the map h: V -> V, h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n, is linear, idempotent with h o h = h, has image n^perp and kernel span(n), satisfies h(n) = 0 and eta(n,h(v)) = 0 for all v in V, and every v in V has the unique decomposition v = -eta(n,v) n + h(v). Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n. The vector w is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity c u relative to the observer n and gamma is its Lorentz factor. (e) Coordinate form. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame and let y be a C^1 future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are t |-> (c t, r(t)), with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3 and, when y is C^2, coordinate acceleration a(t) := w'(t). Then |w(t)| < c, the four-velocity is U = gamma_w (c,w) with gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the four-acceleration is A = gamma_w (d/dt)(gamma_w (c,w)), so that A^0 = gamma_w^4 (w.a)/c and A_vec = gamma_w^2 a + gamma_w^4 (w.a) w/c^2; consequently eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0, with eta(A,A) = 0 if and only if a = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0. For the observer n = e_0 of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to gamma = gamma_w and w_rel = w. (f) Scope. The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel = w. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus.

items.title: Adopted free trajectories of massive particles and the clock hypothesis
items.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending the ideal-clock reading rule of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light to the general worldline calculus of this page: (i) Free trajectories. A massive test particle that is subject to no interaction (a free particle) has as its worldline a straight future timelike line of the affine model: there are an event p in A and a future timelike vector v in V with x(s) = p + (s - s_0) v for all s (the kinematical consequences of this shape for the four-velocity are derived, not assumed, in pthm-sr-four-velocity-norm-and-orthogonality). Interactions, forces and collisions are not part of this assumption: a particle that is not free may have any future timelike worldline admitted by its own dynamical model, and no force law is adopted here. (ii) Clock hypothesis. An ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a piecewise C^1 one with finitely many kinks, reads between any two parameter values the proper-time difference of def-sr-proper-time, with no additional term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative; a kink is an idealization of a finite short acceleration phase whose contribution is included through the integral on the smooth pieces, and the reading does not depend on the choice of the increasing parameter. (iii) Scope and qualification. The assumptions concern ideal point particles, ideal clocks and flat classical spacetime. They are adopted, not proved; they are not consequences of the affine geometry, and no experiment is claimed here to establish them. They inherit the idealizations of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light: real clocks have finite resolution, calibration and apparatus limitations, and real particles are not exactly free.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of straight future timelike lines as the histories of free massive test particles and makes the clock-reading rule applicable to the general worldline class of this page. Obligations: (i) straight future timelike lines are declared objects of the affine model, and each is a future timelike worldline with constant tangent (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); (ii) the reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading with the mathematical proper-time difference, so def-sr-proper-time and its reparametrization invariance are the mathematical suppliers carrying the content, while the identification itself is adopted; (iii) the free-trajectory clause is deliberately silent about interactions and force laws, so it cannot be used to infer conservation laws, mass-shell relations or collision kinematics, which require the separate momentum postulate of the later energy-momentum page; (iv) the clock hypothesis is the assertion that ideal clocks have no acceleration-dependent term, so it must not be presented as following from the geometry. No proof is manufactured; the item is an adopted premise with an exact scope.

items.title: Four-velocity norm and four-acceleration orthogonality for the model's clocks
items.statement: Adopt the postulates of the model: post-sr-inertial-covariance and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light of the spacetime-primitives page together with post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis of this page, and let c and the SI coordinates be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x: I -> A be the history of an ideal clock of the model, a C^1 future timelike worldline (C^2 where acceleration is used), with proper time tau, four-velocity U = dx/dtau and, when x is C^2, four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then: (i) the reading of the ideal clock between parameter values s_1 < s_2 equals tau(s_2) - tau(s_1); (ii) eta(U,U) = -c^2 everywhere, so U is a future unit timelike vector with the unit of a velocity; (iii) if x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0 and A(s) is zero or spacelike, with unit of acceleration; (iv) if the clock is free (no interaction), then its four-velocity is constant along the worldline and A = 0 identically; (v) for an ideal observer at the same event, described by a future unit timelike vector n = U_o/c with eta(n,n) = -1, the clock's speed relative to the observer is |w| = c sqrt(1 - gamma^{-2}) with gamma = -eta(n, U/c) >= 1, so it is strictly less than c, and gamma = 1 exactly when the clock's four-velocity equals the observer's. Scope and qualification: this is a conditional statement about the adopted model; it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and inherits the idealizations of the postulates (ideal point particles, ideal clocks, flat spacetime, no gravitational or quantum effects).
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises; the mathematical content is thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (i) is the clock hypothesis of post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis together with the proper-time definition, restated for the page's worldline calculus. (ii) and (iii) are clauses (a) and (b) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition, with U identified with the clock's four-velocity by the clock hypothesis; the identification supplies the physical meaning of U, the identities are mathematical. (iv) By the free-trajectory clause there are p and future timelike v with x(s) = p + (s - s_0)v; then x' = v is constant, tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(v,v)) is constant and positive, so U = x'/tau' is the constant vector c v/sqrt(-eta(v,v)), and A = U'/tau' = 0. (v) is clause (d) of the mathematical theorem, with the observer vector n allowed to be any future unit timelike vector; post-sr-inertial-covariance licenses the interpretation of observers and clocks as model objects and def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions fixes c and the units of the speed. The proof must not upgrade the conditional statement to a claim about nature and must carry the idealizations to the conclusion.

items.title: Worked example: the clock at rest in an inertial chart
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart of the model with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) consider the worldline x(t) = (c t, a_1, a_2, a_3) of a clock at rest at the spatial position (a_1,a_2,a_3), parametrized by the coordinate time t. Then x'(t) = (c,0,0,0), so -eta(x',x') = c^2 and the proper-time function is tau(t) - tau(t_0) = t - t_0; the four-velocity is U = x'/tau' = (c,0,0,0), with eta(U,U) = -c^2, and the four-acceleration vanishes, A = 0. Relative to the chart's observer e_0 the dimensionless four-velocity is u = U/c = (1,0,0,0) = e_0, so gamma = -eta(e_0,u) = 1 and the relative velocity is w = c h(u)/gamma = 0: the clock is at rest in the chart. This is the c-retained, (-+++) form of the source statement that an object at rest has four-velocity (1,0) and dt/dtau = 1.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: the diagonal form applied to (c,0,0,0) gives -c^2, so the proper-time integrand is the constant c/c = 1 and tau is t - t_0; U = x'/tau' = (c,0,0,0) and U' = 0, so A = 0. The relative-velocity clauses are clauses (c) and (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition evaluated at these vectors. Every step is a finite computation from the definitions.

items.title: Worked example: proper time and four-velocity of a straight worldline at beta = 3/5
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) consider the worldline x(t) = (c t, (3c/5) t, 0, 0), parametrized by coordinate time, which describes a clock moving along the first spatial axis with speed 3c/5. Then x'(t) = (c, 3c/5, 0, 0) and eta(x',x') = -c^2 + (9/25)c^2 = -(16/25)c^2, so sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 4c/5 and tau(t) - tau(t_0) = (4/5)(t - t_0): the moving clock runs slow by the factor 4/5 = 1/gamma with gamma = 5/4. The four-velocity is U = x'/tau' = (5/4)(c, 3c/5, 0, 0) = (5c/4, 3c/4, 0, 0), which satisfies eta(U,U) = -25c^2/16 + 9c^2/16 = -c^2, and the four-acceleration vanishes because U is constant: A = 0. The dimensionless four-velocity is u = U/c = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0); the split of clause (d) with n = e_0 gives gamma = 5/4 and relative velocity w = (3c/5, 0, 0), which is exactly the coordinate velocity.
items.strategy: Direct finite computation: evaluate the diagonal form on x', obtain the constant integrand c^{-1}(4c/5) = 4/5, integrate over [t_0,t], divide to obtain U, and evaluate eta(U,U). The vanishing of A is the constancy of U. The split clauses are clause (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition evaluated at u = (5/4,3/4,0,0) and n = e_0; all numbers are exact rationals.

items.title: Worked example: invariance of elapsed proper time under a cubic reparametrization
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with -eta(d,d) = 25 - 9 = 16 and sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4. (a) The worldline x(s) := s d on the parameter interval [1,8] has x'(s) = d, integrand sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4, and elapsed proper time tau(8) - tau(1) = (1/c) integral_1^8 4 ds = 28/c. (b) The reparametrization phi(u) := u^3 is a strictly increasing C^1 surjection of [1,2] onto [1,8]; the reparametrized curve y(u) := x(u^3) = u^3 d has y'(u) = 3u^2 d, hence sqrt(-eta(y',y')) = 3u^2 sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 12u^2, and elapsed proper time (1/c) integral_1^2 12u^2 du = (4/c)(8 - 1) = 28/c. The two elapsed times agree, as lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance requires, and the proper-time function of x is tau(s) = 4s/c up to an additive constant, with inverse rho(tau) = c(tau - tau_0)/4.
items.strategy: Two independent exact computations of the same elapsed time: in (a) the integrand is the constant 4; in (b) the chain rule gives y' = 3u^2 d and the integrand 12u^2, whose integral over [1,2] is 28. The equality is the concrete instance of the invariance lemma, and the inverse function is read off the linear proper-time function. All arithmetic is rational.

items.title: Worked example: four-velocity and four-acceleration of uniform circular motion
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let R > 0 and omega be real with R|omega| < c and consider the worldline x(t) = (c t, R cos(omega t), R sin(omega t), 0), parametrized by coordinate time: uniform circular motion in the first two spatial coordinates. Then w(t) = (-R omega sin(omega t), R omega cos(omega t), 0) has |w| = R|omega|, so -eta(x',x') = c^2 - R^2 omega^2 and the proper-time factor is tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2 - R^2 omega^2) = 1/gamma with gamma := (1 - R^2 omega^2/c^2)^{-1/2}; the four-velocity is U = gamma (c, w). Since |w| is constant, gamma is constant; the coordinate acceleration is a(t) = (-R omega^2 cos(omega t), -R omega^2 sin(omega t), 0), with |a| = R omega^2 and w.a = 0. By clause (e) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition the four-acceleration is A = gamma^2 a, so A^0 = 0, eta(U,A) = 0 and eta(A,A) = gamma^4 R^2 omega^4 > 0: the four-acceleration is spacelike with magnitude gamma^2 R omega^2. Numerical specialization: if R omega = 3c/5, then gamma = 5/4 and the magnitude of the four-acceleration is gamma^2 R omega^2 = (25/16) R omega^2 = (15 c omega)/16.
items.strategy: Finite computation: differentiate the coordinate path, evaluate the diagonal quadratic form to get tau', read gamma, and apply clause (e) of the theorem with w.a = 0 to obtain A = gamma^2 a; the numerical values are exact rational multiples of c and omega. The acceleration is centripetal and orthogonal to the velocity, so the four-acceleration is orthogonal to the four-velocity by the theorem.

items.title: Worked example: splitting a four-velocity in an observer's rest frame
items.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let the observer be n = e_0 = (1,0,0,0) and let u = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0), a future unit timelike vector: eta(u,u) = -25/16 + 9/16 = -1. Then gamma = -eta(n,u) = 5/4 >= 1, h(u) = u + eta(n,u) n = u - (5/4)(1,0,0,0) = (0, 3/4, 0, 0) lies in n^perp = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), and the relative velocity is w = c h(u)/gamma = (0, 3c/5, 0, 0). One checks u = gamma (n + w/c) = (5/4)(1, 3/5, 0, 0) and |w|^2 = 9c^2/25 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) = c^2 (1 - 16/25). Also h(h(u)) = h(u) and eta(n,h(u)) = 0. This four-velocity is the one of the clock with coordinate velocity (3c/5, 0, 0) in ex-sr-proper-time-of-a-straight-worldline.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation of clauses (c) and (d) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition on the displayed vectors: the projection, its idempotence and its orthogonality to n, the split u = gamma(n + w/c) and the identity |w|^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) are each finite computations with rational numbers.

items.title: Counterexample: a future null curve has no proper-time parametrization
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'every regular C^1 curve of the model admits a proper-time parametrization, with strictly increasing proper-time function and normalized timelike four-velocity'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let k := (1,1,0,0), a future null vector with eta(k,k) = -1 + 1 = 0, and let x(s) := p + s k be the corresponding future null straight line. Then x'(s) = k is nonzero and future null for every s, so x is a regular future null curve in the sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, but the proper-time integrand is sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 0 identically: the associated integral is constant, its derivative vanishes, there is no strictly increasing reparametrization by it, and no normalized four-velocity U with eta(U,U) = -c^2 can be attached to the curve, since every tangent vector is null. The coordinate speed of the curve is c (x^0 = c s and x^1 = s give x^1 = c t), so the curve does describe a light ray; it simply has no massive proper-time parametrization.
items.strategy: Direct computation: eta(k,k) = 0 makes the integrand vanish identically, so the proper-time function is constant and cannot be inverted; the tangent vectors are null, so no timelike unit normalization exists. The example is the concrete reason why def-sr-proper-time carries the future timelike hypothesis and why null rays need their own parametrization. All steps are finite evaluations of the diagonal form.

items.title: Counterexample: the proper-time integrand of a spacelike curve is not real
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'the formula tau(b) - tau(a) = c^{-1} integral_a^b sqrt(-eta(x',x')) ds assigns an elapsed clock time to every regular C^1 curve of the model'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (1,2,0,0), a spacelike displacement with eta(d,d) = -1 + 4 = 3 > 0, and let x(s) := p + s d. Then x'(s) = d is spacelike, -eta(x',x') = -3 < 0, and the square root of a negative real number is not defined: the proper-time construction of def-sr-proper-time produces no real value on this curve. The geometric spacing along the curve is governed by the spacelike length sqrt(eta(d,d)) = sqrt(3) per unit parameter, not by a clock reading: a spacelike interval is not elapsed clock time, and such curves are the reason def-sr-proper-time carries the future timelike hypothesis.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: the diagonal form on d gives +3, so the integrand -eta(d,d) is negative and has no real square root; hence the claim that the construction assigns a clock time to every regular curve is false. The final clause records which hypothesis of the definition excludes the case and that the spacelike length of the curve is a different quantity, not an elapsed time.

items.title: Counterexample: a past-directed parametrization of a timelike line is not a worldline
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'if a C^1 curve parametrizes a straight timelike line, then it is a future timelike worldline of the model and the proper-time construction gives the clock reading of its history'. Counterexample: in an inertial chart with eta_0 = diag(-1,1,1,1) let d := (5,3,0,0), a future timelike displacement with -eta(d,d) = 16, and let x(s) := p - s d for s in [0,1]. Then x'(s) = -d is past timelike for every s, so x is not a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); but the integrand sqrt(-eta(x',x')) = 4 is the same as for the future-parametrized line s |-> p + s d, so the proper-time integral alone does not distinguish the two parametrizations. The model's clock reading attaches to the future-directed history: the same image with the parametrization s |-> p + s d is the worldline, and x is its orientation reversal. This is why the parametrization, and not merely the image of the curve, is part of the definition of a worldline.
items.strategy: Direct evaluation: eta(-d,-d) = eta(d,d) = -16, so the integrand is identical for the two parametrizations; the future/past alternative is decided by the time orientation of the model, not by the sign of eta(x',x'). Every step is a finite computation.
